Description: Nominal companion of myszkowski_2018_spmls: SPM-LS (last series of Raven's SPM), 12 items, 499 respondents; text = option chosen (1-8, 7 distractors + key), resp = correct.

Reference: Sirota, M., & Juanchich, M. (2018). Effect of response format on cognitive reflection: Validating a two- and four-option multiple choice question version of the Cognitive Reflection Test. Behavior Research Methods, 50, 2511-2522.

Description: Nominal companion of suarez_2026_statistics: university statistics exam, 431 students, 85-item bank; text = text of the option chosen (Spanish; option order was randomised), resp = correct.

Description: Nominal companion of geography (slepemapy.cz adaptive geography practice, 2012-2015): 10.1M answers, 91,331 learners, 1,458 places; text = id of the place chosen, or dont_know; options offered in trial_options, place names in itemcov_place_name.

Notes: Built from answer.csv (2015-05-21 dump), which data/geography.R scores but drops place_answered. Carries date (inserted) and NA for the rt sentinel itself; the core table rebuild is queued in #2558. Script data/nominal/geography.py.

Description: Nominal companion of cifar10h: CIFAR-10H human labels of the 10,000 CIFAR-10 test images, 2,571 annotators; text = class chosen (10 classes), resp = 1 if it matches the CIFAR-10 label (itemcov_true_category).
Reference: Peterson, J. C., Battleday, R. M., Griffiths, T. L., & Russakovsky, O. (2019). Human uncertainty makes classification more robust. Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 9617-9626.
Notes: Non-commercial share-alike (ruled #2655). Same rows as the core cifar10h with resp_raw renamed to text. Script data/cifar10h.py.

Description: SemEval-2013 Task 7 SciEntsBank: grade 3-6 students' written answers to FOSS/ASK science assessment questions, 3,026 students x 195 questions (sparse); text = graders' 5-way accuracy label (correct / partially_correct_incomplete / contradictory / irrelevant / non_domain), resp = 1 if correct, answer_text = the student's answer.
Reference: Dzikovska, M. O., Nielsen, R., Brew, C., Leacock, C., Giampiccolo, D., Bentivogli, L., Clark, P., Dagan, I., & Dang, H. T. (2013). SemEval-2013 Task 7: The Joint Student Response Analysis and 8th Recognizing Textual Entailment Challenge. Proceedings of the 7th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation (SemEval 2013), 263-274.
Notes: Share-alike. SciEntsBank half only (Beetle under the 100-id floor). id = module_student (students are module-specific, Nielsen et al. 2008); 36 answers with no student number (all of ME_28b) dropped. Commit 5157c69f. Script data/nominal/semeval2013_scientsbank.py.

Description: Nominal companion of navarrete_2023_policy_approval_france, same rows, ids, items and dates: Mon Programme 2022 (monprogramme2022.org), an online platform run before the 2022 French presidential election (data to 6 June 2022) offering 120 policy proposals taken from the candidates' programmes. 1,629 participants x 120 proposals, 120,755 rows; panels of 4, 5 or 6 (3 in 267 rows, outside the design), alternating with a rank panel. Participants built a personal government programme from the candidates' policy proposals: in panels of k proposals (k assigned at random per participant, cov_panel_size) they pressed approve, disapprove or blank for each. text = the button pressed, approve / disapprove / blank, all three kept as categories (blank is an observed choice here, not a missing response); resp = the core table's score, 1 approve, 0 disapprove, empty for blank. item = the deposit's proposal id; the proposal text (in three languages), its category are in the deposit's Dataset 5 (set_proposals_france.tab), keyed by the same id. Repeated id x item rows are kept as recorded (mostly a panel stored twice a fraction of a second apart; some proposals answered again later); date (Unix seconds) orders them. Covariates: panel size, platform language, the authors' bot flag (cov_suspicious) and pre-launch flag, and from the optional demographic popup (latest record) political orientation 1-5 left to right, age group, sex, urban/rural zone, education, location (department code), as the deposit's codes (meanings in the script header). No participant excluded (the authors drop the 103 participants here flagged as suspicious). Voluntary online participants, not a sample of the electorate. The rank screen of the same platform (Dataset 2) is not in IRW. Script data/nominal/navarrete_2023_policy.py (core table: data/navarrete_2023_policy.py).
Reference: Navarrete C, Macedo M, Colley R, Zhang J, Ferrada N, Mello ME, Lira R, Bastos-Filho C, Grandi U, Lang J, Hidalgo CA (2023). Understanding political divisiveness using online participation data from the 2022 French and Brazilian presidential elections. Nature Human Behaviour, 8, 137-148. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-023-01755-x
Notes: Licence fields mirror the core navarrete_2023_policy_approval_france row (#3511). Built by data/nominal/navarrete_2023_policy.py as a rename of the core table's resp_raw to text. Description: Nominal companion of polis_2014_seattle_min_wage, same rows, ids, items and dates: Polis conversation '$15/hour'. Every vote in the export's votes.csv is a row: a participant who voted on a statement again has a row per vote, ordered by date (Unix seconds); the latest is the standing vote. itemcov_moderated = the statement's moderation status at export (1 accepted, 0 unmoderated, -1 moderated out); votes on moderated-out statements are kept. itemcov_author_id = the id of the statement's author; Polis usually records an agree for the author on submission, so many statements carry only the author's vote. No covariates.

Participants wrote short statements and voted on other participants' statements, shown one at a time, with agree, disagree or pass/unsure. text = the button pressed, agree / disagree / pass, all three kept as categories (pass is an observed choice here, not a missing response); resp = the core table's score, 1 agree, 0 disagree, empty for pass. item = the deposit's comment-id; the statement text is in the deposit's comments.csv, keyed by the same id. Every vote in the export's votes.csv is a row: a participant who voted on a statement again has a row per vote, ordered by date (Unix seconds); the latest is the standing vote. itemcov_moderated = the statement's moderation status at export (1 accepted, 0 unmoderated, -1 moderated out); votes on moderated-out statements are kept. itemcov_author_id = the id of the statement's author; Polis usually records an agree for the author on submission, so many statements carry only the author's vote. No covariates.
Reference: The Computational Democracy Project. Polis open data: Protecting and Restoring NZ's Biodiversity (openData/scoop-hivemind.biodiversity). https://github.com/compdemocracy/openData. Data was gathered using the Polis software (compdemocracy.org/polis) and is sub-licensed under CC BY 4.0 with Attribution to The Computational Democracy Project. The data and more information about how the data was collected can be found at the following link(s): https://compdemocracy.org/case-studies/2019-scoop-hivemind-biodiversity https://github.com/compdemocracy/openData/tree/master/scoop-hivemind.biodiversity
